description: Implement a token bucket rate limiter (fractional refill over elapsed time, capped at capacity) driven via a stdin command protocol
prompts: Create a C program in limiter.c implementing a token bucket rate limiter, driven by commands read from stdin (one per line) until EOF: `init CAPACITY REFILL_RATE` initializes the bucket (both doubles; the bucket starts full with CAPACITY tokens); `allow NOW` (NOW is a double, seconds) refills the bucket based on elapsed time since the last call (REFILL_RATE tokens per second, capped at CAPACITY - never above it even after a long idle gap), then - if at least 1 token is available - consumes exactly 1 and prints `1`; otherwise prints `0` and consumes nothing. Assume `init` is called exactly once, before any `allow`.
name: add_c_token_bucket_limiter

test_setup_files.test_limiter.py:
import subprocess
subprocess.run(['gcc', '-std=c11', '-Wall', 'limiter.c', '-o', 'limiter_bin'], check=True)

def run(commands):
    text = '\n'.join(commands) + '\n'
    proc = subprocess.run(['./limiter_bin'], input=text, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
    assert proc.returncode == 0, f'nonzero exit: {proc.returncode}, stderr={proc.stderr[-400:]}'
    return [l.strip() for l in proc.stdout.strip('\n').split('\n') if proc.stdout.strip('\n')]

out = run(['init 3 1', 'allow 0', 'allow 0', 'allow 0', 'allow 0'])
assert out == ['1', '1', '1', '0'], f'starts full and drains: got {out}'

out = run(['init 3 1', 'allow 0', 'allow 0', 'allow 0', 'allow 0.5', 'allow 1.0', 'allow 1.0'])
assert out == ['1', '1', '1', '0', '1', '0'], f'refills over time: got {out}'

out = run(['init 2 1', 'allow 0', 'allow 0', 'allow 1000', 'allow 1000', 'allow 1000'])
assert out == ['1', '1', '1', '1', '0'], f'refill caps at capacity: got {out}'

print('PASS')
